stem: A 35-year-old man has had a vasectomy reversed and has been unable to father a child for 18 months. His testosterone, FSH and LH are normal and there is no varicocele. Semen analysis shows sperm that clump together tail to tail and move poorly, though the count is adequate.
oneliner: 35M + vasectomy reversal + infertile 18 months + normal hormones, no varicocele + sperm clumped and poorly motile → what immune consequence?
ask: Which process best explains his infertility?

options.B: Leydig cell failure with low testosterone

whyNot.A: A **tumor** would not make sperm **clump tail to tail**
whyNot.B: **Low testosterone** is excluded by his **normal hormones**
whyNot.D: **Retrograde ejaculation** gives low volume and sperm in post-void urine, not clumping

why: Vasectomy lets sperm leak from the blocked duct, exposing **sperm antigens** normally hidden behind the **blood-testis barrier**. The body makes **antisperm antibodies** that **agglutinate** sperm and impair motility, so he is **infertile** despite normal hormones.
chain: Vasectomy: sperm leak from the blocked duct
Haploid sperm antigens meet the immune system

idea.rule: Breaking a hidden-antigen barrier turns self into foreign.
also: Mumps orchitis and testicular trauma can do the same
Spermatic granuloma follows sperm leakage after vasectomy
Mixed antiglobulin reaction test detects antisperm antibodies

stem: A 45-year-old man has generalized swelling and frothy urine. He now notices a new swelling in the left scrotum that feels like a bag of worms and enlarges when he bears down. It does not empty when he lies down, and a flank mass is felt on the left.
oneliner: 45M + new left bag-of-worms scrotal swelling + enlarges with straining + stays full lying down + edema and flank mass → what to look for?
ask: Which underlying problem should be sought next?

whyNot.A: Gives a **smooth fluid sac** (hydrocele) or hernia, not a tangle of veins, and has no link to his **kidney findings**
whyNot.B: Causes **infertility with normal veins**; it does not produce a bag-of-worms swelling
whyNot.C: Presents as a **firm, painless testicular mass**; it does not enlarge with straining like dilated veins
whyNot.D: Bowel in the canal gives a bulge that **reduces when lying down** and has bowel sounds, not worm-like veins

answer: Left renal vein obstruction (thrombus or tumor)
why: Because the **left testicular vein empties into the left renal vein**, obstruction there (renal vein thrombosis or **renal cell carcinoma**) raises pressure in the plexus. His **adult onset**, **failure to empty when supine**, **nephrotic picture and flank mass** call for imaging of the left kidney and renal vein.
chain: Obstruction of the left renal vein
Pressure rises in the left gonadal vein
Left varicocele that does not empty when lying down
Look for renal thrombus or tumor

idea.rule: A sudden or non-decompressing varicocele in an adult is a sign of an obstructed venous drainage, not just a local valve problem.
also: Right varicocele suggests IVC obstruction or retroperitoneal mass
Left gonadal vein drains to the left renal vein; right drains to the IVC
Renal cell carcinoma invades the renal vein
Nephrotic syndrome predisposes to renal vein thrombosis

stem: A 28-year-old woman at 37 weeks of gestation is lying flat for a fetal heart monitor strip when she becomes dizzy and pale. Her blood pressure reads 80/60 mm Hg, and the fetal heart rate is normal. Her blood pressure was normal when she sat in the waiting room, and she has no bleeding or abdominal pain.
oneliner: 28F + 37 weeks pregnant + dizzy lying flat + BP 80/60 supine, normal sitting + no bleeding or pain → what corrects it?
ask: Which action should be taken now?

options.B: Turn her onto her left side
options.E: Keep her supine with legs raised

whyNot.A: Does not lift the uterus off the vein, and the **uterus still compresses** the cava
whyNot.C: Not needed: the fall occurs **only when supine**, with a **normal fetal heart rate**
whyNot.D: Used for **preeclampsia seizures**; her problem is **low** pressure from position
whyNot.E: The **uterus still sits on the cava**, so return of blood stays reduced

why: In the third trimester the **gravid uterus compresses the inferior vena cava** when she lies on her back, lowering venous return and cardiac output. **Turning onto the left side** lifts the uterus off the cava and restores blood pressure.
chain: Gravid uterus lies on the IVC when supine
Cardiac output and blood pressure drop
Left lateral position frees the cava

idea.rule: A pregnant woman late in gestation should not lie flat on her back, and positioning fixes supine hypotension.
also: Left lateral tilt during cesarean or resuscitation
The IVC lies to the right of the aorta
Reduced venous return lowers preload and cardiac output

stem: A 29-year-old woman has had periods every 2 to 3 months since menarche and has acne and dark hair on her chin. Her BMI is 34. Pelvic ultrasound shows enlarged ovaries with many peripheral follicles, and pregnancy tests are negative. She is diagnosed with polycystic ovary syndrome and asks where to begin.
oneliner: 29F + BMI 34 + oligomenorrhea since menarche + acne and hirsutism + polycystic ovaries on ultrasound → first step?
ask: What is the most appropriate first management step?

options.D: Diet and exercise for weight loss

whyNot.A: An outdated **surgical** option for resistant infertility, not a first step
whyNot.B: Treats only the **hair**; does not address **insulin resistance** or cycle regularity
whyNot.C: **Suppresses** the axis and induces menopause-like state; not used for PCOS
whyNot.E: Reserved for **morbid obesity** after lifestyle measures fail; her BMI is 34

why: In **obese women with PCOS**, **weight loss through diet and exercise** lowers **insulin resistance**, which reduces ovarian androgen output and often **restores ovulation**. Drugs such as combined oral contraceptives or metformin are added later.

idea.rule: In PCOS with obesity, lowering insulin resistance comes before drugs or surgery.
also: Combined oral contraceptives for cycle control and hirsutism
Clomiphene or letrozole to induce ovulation
